10:1: <section date.revised="0" date.updated="0"><metadata.block metadata.store="yes"><metadata field="classification"><value>IMM.IV.5.g Immigration and citizenship—Exclusion and removal—Removal from Canada—Appeals and judicial review</value></metadata></metadata.block><section.front date.updated="0"><outline.name.block toc.include="y" date.updated="0"><label date.updated="0">§</label><designator date.updated="0">10:1</designator><name date.updated="0">Executive Summary</name></outline.name.block></section.front><section.body date.updated="0"><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">As described in Chapter 9, there are various types of removal orders and numerous reasons for which they may be issued. Despite an erosion of appeal rights in successive amendments to the <ital>IRPA</ital>, certain permanent residents (in some cases foreign nationals) in receipt of removal orders do retain the right to appeal these removal orders. Appeals are heard by the Immigration Appeal Division (“IAD”) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (“IRB”). Filing an appeal for a removal order will often stop the removal process until a decision on the appeal is made. This chapter will examine the statutory framework surrounding removal order appeals, appeal eligibility, and the various outcomes available during the appeal process. The chapter will then specifically focus on appeal ineligibility at the IAD. Practical tips for handling immigration appeals involving criminality will be canvassed. Finally, a key component of certain criminality appeals involving foreign convictions is<?WGXPPrightHandPageStart sp=";;3" nep=";;5" hyphenated="y" folio="10-3" backFolio="10-4" backBlank="n" releaseNumber="4" releaseDate="2023;12;31"  ?> an equivalency analysis. An equivalency analysis is undertaken where persons are found to be inadmissible as a result of having committed or been convicted of crimes/acts in other countries beside to determine if the crime/acts are equivalent to an offence under an Act of Parliament in Canada.</para.text></para></section.body></section>

Cannot?</name></outline.name.block></section.front><section.body date.updated="0"><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="0">Permanent residents, Convention refugees, protected persons and foreign nationals with a permanent resident visa who have been ordered removed from Canada may submit an appeal, as per ss. 63(2) and (3) of the <ital>IRPA</ital>.</para.text></para><stat.structure date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">In comparison, ss. 64(1) and (2) of the <ital>IRPA</ital> states that an individual cannot appeal a removal order if they have been found An overview of the Removal Order appeal process can be found at: <cite finder="manual" type="url"><ref normalpub="webref" ref.id="I23449e307a3c11eeae2bcd9e4a381e45">https://irb.gc.ca/en/making-immigration-appeal/Pages/immapp-bc2.aspx</ref></cite>.</para.text></para></footnote.body></footnote></name></outline.name.block></section.front><section.body date.updated="0"><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">An appeal in most cases must be filed within 30 days of receiving the decision to issue a removal order. An appeal is initiated by filing a Notice of Appeal form, which is usually provided along with the removal order, along with a copy of the removal order that was received. The Respondent must produce the Appeal Record (disclosure) within either 30 or 60 days following the filing of the Notice of Appeal.<footnote date.updated="0"><footnote.reference date.updated="0">2</footnote.reference><footnote.body date.updated="0"><para date.updated="20231124"><para.text date.updated="0">For further information, see sections 20–23 of the <ital>Immigration Appeal Division Rules</ital> (SOR/2022-277).</para.text></para></footnote.body></footnote> With respect to responding documentary disclosure, the appellant must make two copies of each document (including any photographs or audio-visual files). The appellant has a chance to provide documents in response to the documents from the Minister's counsel — these must be received no later than 10 days before the hearing.<footnote date.updated="0"><footnote.reference date.updated="0">4</footnote.reference><footnote.body date.updated="0"><para date.trace="20231124" date.updated="20231124"><para.text date.updated="0">See section 27 of the <ital>Immigration Appeal Division Rules, 2022</ital> (SOR/2022-277) for the time limit to respond to evidence.</para.text></para></footnote.body></footnote></para.text></para><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">With respect to witnesses, no later than 30 days before the hearing,  any party who wishes to call a witness must provide a list of witnesses, which must provide the following information:</para.text><list list.style="block" date.updated="0"><list.item date.updated="0"><name.block toc.include="y" date.updated="0"><designator date.updated="0">1</designator></name.block><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="0">The witness' contact information (address, telephone and fax numbers);</para.text></para></list.item><list.item date.updated="0"><name.block toc.include="y" date.updated="0"><designator date.updated="0">2</designator></name.block><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">A brief statement of the purpose and substance of the witness' testimony;</para.text></para></list.item><list.item date.updated="0"><name.block toc.include="y" date.updated="0"><designator date.updated="0">3</designator></name.block><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">The party's relationship to the witness; and</para.text></para></list.item><list.item date.updated="0"><name.block toc.include="y" date.updated="0"><designator date.updated="0">4</designator></name.block><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">Whether the party wants the witness to testify remotely, and if so, by which means (i.e., must be live telecommunication such as telephone, via videoconference, etc.).</para.text></para></list.item></list></para><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="20231124">As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, hearings were shifted online to proceed by videoconference, and this has remained the default mode of hearing.<footnote date.updated="0"><footnote.reference date.updated="0">4.30</footnote.reference><footnote.body date.updated="0"><para date.updated="0"><para.text date.updated="0">See the following link explaining the available hearing formats at the IRB: <cite finder="manual" type="url"><ref normalpub="webref" ref.id="I2345afa07a3c11eeae2bcd9e4a381e45">https://irb.gc.ca/en/legal-policy/procedures/hearings-at-the-IRB/Pages/request-hybrid-or-in-person-hearing.aspx</ref></cite>.
